industry: Mid-market HR analytics SaaS for 200-2,000 employee firms in North America

factors: HRIS integrations take 12-18 months to build
AI tooling lowers the cost of a first dashboard
Buyers ask for SOC 2 before a pilot
new_entrants.evidence: Four funded entrants in 2025; two shut down within a year citing integration cost

factors: Three HRIS vendors hold about 70% of the segment's employee records
Their partner APIs are rate-limited and priced per call
supplier_power.evidence: The largest HRIS vendor raised partner API fees 40% in 2026

factors: Fragmented buyers, top 10 customers are 18% of revenue
Switching requires re-mapping two years of history
buyer_power.evidence: Gross retention 91% in 2025; average discount at renewal 6%

factors: HRIS vendors bundle native analytics at no extra cost
Spreadsheets plus BI tools cover basic headcount reporting
substitute_threat.evidence: Native analytics cited in 11 of 26 lost deals in 2025

factors: Six direct competitors, none above 15% share
Price competition mainly on seat bands
competitive_rivalry.evidence: Analyst segment report, Q1 2026; win rate stable at 31%

strategy_implications.move: Lead with cross-system analysis the bundled HRIS dashboards cannot do
Add a second ingestion path (payroll and ATS exports) to cut dependence on HRIS APIs
Raise switching cost with saved benchmark history and board-pack templates
